matched_queries: UK employment guidance: Eligibility and qualifying service for paternity leave and unpaid parental leave, including entitlement from starting employment.
Discover UK employment guidance for Paternity leave: entitlement. Task relevance is separate from current law, commencement and a need to edit.

passages.quote:
Employees must be one of the following, the:

father

husband or partner of the mother (or adopter)

child’s adopter

intended parent (if they’re having a baby through a surrogacy arrangement)

Employees must also:

be classed as an employee (Paternity Leave only)

be employed by you up to the date the child is born (or placed with the adopter) (Paternity Pay only)

be on your payroll and earn at least £129 a week (gross) in an 8 week ‘relevant period’ (Paternity Pay only)

give you the correct notice

be taking time off to look after the child or their partner

be responsible for the child’s upbringing

have been continuously employed by you for at least 26 weeks up to any day in the ‘qualifying week’ (Paternity Pay only)

The qualifying week is the 15th week before the baby is due. This is different if the employee is adopting.

Employees are eligible for Paternity Leave from their first day of employment.

Use the Paternity Pay calculator to check an employee’s eligibility and work out their relevant period, notice period and Paternity Pay.

There are special rules for some employee situations, for example if they leave or become sick.

If the child is born early

If the child is born early, the employee is still eligible for Paternity Pay if they would have worked for you continuously for at least 26 weeks by the qualifying week. They are eligible for Paternity Leave from their first day of employment.

Employees in surrogacy arrangements

Parents intending to have a child through a surrogacy arrangement may be eligible for Statutory Paternity Leave and Pay.

If you ask, they must give you a written statement to confirm that they’ve applied or intend to apply for a parental order in the 6 months after the baby’s birth.
